item.title: Yuan’s Recent Calm May End on Seasonal Factors, Analysts Say
item.description: The yuan’s recent calm run may be nearing an end as September approaches, with typically strong fall exports and other seasonal factors expected to lift the Chinese currency, analysts say.

item.title: Hong Kong Tech Index Set for Overhaul With More Firms, AI Focus
item.description: Hong Kong’s main technology stock benchmark is set for a revamp to include more companies representing the fast-growing artificial intelligence and robotics sectors, a long‑awaited move for investors eager to better capture China’s technological advances.

item.title: Hong Kong May Expand Tax Breaks to Trading Firms, FT Says
item.description: Hong Kong regulators may include trading firms such as Jane Street and Citadel Securities in a sweeping new tax regime that has already boosted the city’s appeal to hedge funds, according to a report from the Financial Times.

item.title: Nifty 50 Inclusion Could Boost BSE as NSE Gears Up For Listing
item.description: The inclusion could lead to passive flows of about $741 million into BSE.

item.title: New Bank Indonesia Chief Faces Test of Driving Growth While Defending Autonomy
item.description: When Destry Damayanti was appointed Indonesia’s acting central bank governor two weeks ago, one of her first meetings that day was at the finance minister’s office.

item.title: Amkor Is Said to Mull Stake Sale in $1.5 Billion China Unit
item.description: Amkor Technology Inc., a provider of outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing services, is considering options including selling a stake in its China business, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: China’s Teapots May Boost Iran Oil Buying as Stockpiles Dwindle
item.description: Shrinking regional oil stockpiles held by China’s independent refiners in Shandong province may spur increased buying of Iranian crude, offering Tehran a needed boost after a period of slow sales.

item.title: Apple’s Glass-Centric 20th-Anniversary iPhone Remains on Track for 2027
item.description: Apple Inc. is still planning to offer a glass-centric overhaul of the iPhone for the device’s 20th anniversary, people familiar with the matter said, countering an analyst report that the move had been canceled.

item.title: Australian Business Confidence Drops on Middle East Uncertainty
item.description: Australian business confidence snapped three months of gains as uncertainty over the Middle East conflict and persistent energy price strength weighed on the outlook.

item.title: Ex-RBI Chief Says Structural Issues Driving Money From India
item.description: India’s waning appeal among foreign investors means short-term measures to attract capital are unlikely to stem the rupee’s weakness, former central bank Governor Duvvuri Subbarao said, adding to calls from other economists for deeper structural reforms.

item.title: Kioxia Says Investment Vehicle for SK Hynix Is Top Shareholder
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp.’s biggest shareholder is an investment vehicle that holds shares claimed by rival SK Hynix Inc.

item.title: Tencent’s WorkBuddy Sparks AI Turnaround Hopes After Stock Rout
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s early success with WorkBuddy may give the Chinese Internet giant a chance to catch up after lagging peers in the artificial intelligence race for the past few years.

item.title: Anthropic Strikes $9 Billion Cloud Deal With Riot Platforms
item.description: Anthropic PBC has struck a $9.1 billion deal with Riot Platforms Inc., a Bitcoin mining company that recently began selling AI data center capacity, people familiar with the matter said, underscoring the Claude maker’s efforts to secure enough computing to meet its customers’ demand.

item.title: AI Boom Set to Drive Singapore Growth as High as 5.5% This Year
item.description: Singapore upgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast anew as the artificial intelligence boom lifts trade and manufacturing, offsetting the drag from continued fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Colombia Inflation Unexpectedly Slows, Easing Pressure on Rates
item.description: Colombia’s inflation rate cooled last month, offering some relief to the central bank after policymakers recently surprised investors by keeping borrowing costs unchanged.

item.title: Gold Climbs Above $4,400 as Traders Turn Focus to US Inflation
item.description: Gold advanced to a two-month high above $4,400 an ounce ahead of a key US inflation report that could provide fresh clues to the Federal Reserve’s appetite for an interest-rate hike.

item.title: Intel Is Said to Near Share Sale Upsize to Raise $20 Billion
item.description: Intel Corp. is seeking to increase the amount it’s raising in a share sale to about $20 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, a third more than it was targeting when it announced the deal Monday morning.

item.title: UK Consumers Stay at Home to Avoid Extreme Heat, Retailers Say
item.description: British shoppers retreated during the July heat wave, prioritizing small treats and cutting back elsewhere as the recent consumer boost showed signs of fading.

item.title: Traders Are Piling Into Taiwan Dollar Options to Bet on Rebound
item.description: Currency traders are stepping up bullish options bets on the Taiwan dollar, signaling a shift in sentiment after the currency suffered its worst July since 2015.

item.title: Asian Bank Stocks Rally as Investors Seek Safety From Volatile AI Trade
item.description: Asian banks are staging one of their strongest stock rallies in decades, a trend that may continue as investors look for a safer bet in the face of the volatile AI trade.

item.title: Google’s AI Team Tells Job Seekers Its HR Filters Are Unreliable
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google pitches its artificial intelligence tools to corporate clients as a way to more quickly sift through a mountain of job applications to find the most promising candidates. Some of its own AI researchers don’t want to rely on these tools when recruiting.

item.title: SEC Alleges Fund Adviser Misled Investors in Pre-IPO Schemes
item.description: Investment adviser Adit Ventures and co-founder Eric Munson were accused by the US Securities and Exchange Commission of making false claims about investments and overcharging clients with millions of dollars in undisclosed fees to buy shares of companies including SpaceX and Klarna before they were offered to the public.

item.title: Trump Media Losses Hit $238 Million as Firm Pivots to Fast Feeds
item.description: Donald Trump’s social media company posted steeper losses as it careened from a big cryptocurrency bet into a controversial new line of business selling faster access to market-moving posts from the US president.

item.title: Oil Holds Gains, Asian Stocks Set for Muted Open: Markets Wrap
item.description: Oil held onto a rally as hopes faded for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Asian stocks were set for a muted start ahead of key US inflation reports.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 11
item.description: Oil held a three-day gain after President Donald Trump made sweeping new demands on Iran, clouding the outlook for a deal to reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: 777 Partners Files Bankruptcy After Creditors’ Liquidation Push
item.description: Alternative investment firm 777 Partners has filed for bankruptcy weeks after creditors sought to liquidate what’s left of the company that began unloading its assets more than a year ago.

item.title: Chicago Taps Fitch Senior Director as New CFO Amid Rash of Exits
item.description: Chicago is hiring Ashlee Gabrysch, a senior director at Fitch Ratings, as its next chief financial officer, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: AI Stock Heavy ETF Risks Spread to Broader Equity Market
item.description: A growing share of equity leverage is riding on the same AI names, many of which have seen historic swings.

item.title: Five Takeaways From Zuckerberg’s 6,500-Word Manifesto on AI
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg touted his views on artificial intelligence in a 6,500-word essay published Monday, emphasizing his belief that wider access to AI models is key to the industry’s future.

item.title: Webtoon Buys $100 Million Share in Game Studio to Expand Reach
item.description: Webtoon Entertainment Inc. is buying a majority stake in a Korean gaming studio for about $100 million, in its latest push to expand a content portfolio that includes web comics, anime and gaming.
